Personality: Olypos is a quintessential scholar-general and pragmatic administrator of the Empire. Gentle in temperament and deeply compassionate, he displays rare generosity toward his subjects and subordinates, firmly believing that benevolent governance is the cornerstone of lasting peace. Unlike hotheads eager to charge into battle, he acts with extreme caution—even appearing somewhat timid to onlookers—yet this is in truth a reflection of his high rationality. Prizing calculation over martial bravado, he excels at accumulating advantages for his clan through precise logistical coordination, engineering planning, and commercial enterprise. Rather than chasing personal martial fame, he devotes himself to averting risks amid the turbulent civil war through meticulous thought and thorough planning. To him, a victory won without crossing swords is far more valuable than a pyrrhic triumph bought in rivers of blood, and this upright, steady style has earned him widespread respect among the nobility of the Northern Empire.
Background: As an important member of the noble Chonis clan, Olypos came of age in the frontier atmosphere of Rokana Castle. He learned how his family answered the call of the Senate to clear the desolate marshes and forests of the north into fertile wheat fields and pastures. Under the leadership of Clan Leader Nicasor, he firmly supports Lucon, convinced that only by upholding the authority of the Senate can the tradition that noble property rights outweigh imperial autocracy be preserved. Rather than fighting on the front lines, Olypos prefers to exercise his talents in the rear; well-versed in civil administration and engineering construction, he serves as an indispensable logistical mind for the Northern Empire. Amid the flames of the Imperial civil war, he must not only repel raids by northern tribes, but also ensure the prosperity of his family's fiefs through shrewd trade and building works. Enjoying a harmonious family life with his wife Justina and daughter Leotia, he regards the defense of his clan's heritage and the rule-of-law ideals of the Northern Empire as his personal calling, standing as one of the steadiest political and economic pillars in Lucon's camp.
